article.headline: Insmed Surges 18.7% On Report Sanofi Is Weighing A Takeover
article.deck: The jump carried Insmed through a 137.80 buy point in a 15-week cup, and at 142.15 it sits inside the buy range that runs to 144.69.
body: Insmed rose 22.35, or 18.7%, to 142.15 as of 11:43 a.m. Mountain, clearing the 137.80 buy point of a 15-week cup that corrected 32.7% from its August 6 rim to an October 23 low. The stock is 3.2% past the buy point and inside the buy range, which tops out at 144.69. It has already traded 3.39x its 50-day average volume and is on pace for 5.23x.

The cup formed after a bigger slide: the stock is still well below its 212.75 high of Dec. 2, 2025, and 33.2% off that 52-week peak. The 21-day line is at 115.87 and the 50-day at 110.81; the stock is 28.3% above the 50-day, yet it reads only 0.32 ATRs from the 21-day line, so the move is not stretched on that measure. Insmed ranks 93 of 99 on the desk's list, and the RS line is 36.6% below its high. The stock is up 51.2% in a month but still down 18.3% this year.

The company is not yet profitable. It lost 0.46 a share in the September quarter, after losses of 0.06, 0.76 and 1.54 in the three quarters before. Revenue climbed each quarter, from 263.8 million to 306.0 million, 425.5 million and 524.4 million, up 268.4% from a year earlier in the latest. The market cap is about 31.18 billion and the forward P/E is 221.45.
The catalyst is deal talk. Proactive and TIKR reported that Sanofi is weighing a potential takeover, and Stocktwits said the stock was on track for its best day in more than three months.
A close back under 137.80 would put the breakout in the stalled column; a run past 144.69 ends the buy range.
article.watch: Whether Insmed closes inside the 137.80 to 144.69 buy range as the takeover report plays out.

article.headline: Intuitive Surgical Falls 2.4% As Sales Grow But Earnings Slide
article.deck: Still 1.4% above its 405.44 flat-base buy point and inside the range to 425.71, but the stock has dropped under its 50-day and 200-day lines.
body: Intuitive Surgical fell 9.93, or 2.4%, to 411.02 as of 11:43 a.m. Mountain, slipping under its 50-day line at 422.99. The stock broke out of a five-week flat base, 14.8% deep, past a 405.44 buy point on Sept. 28, and 38 sessions later it is just 1.4% above that level and still inside the buy range that runs to 425.71. Volume is light, on pace for 0.55x its 50-day average.

The breakout never went anywhere. The stock is 2.8% below the 50-day line, 4.0% below the 200-day at 428.09 and 6.0% under the 21-day line at 437.06, a reading of -0.84 ATRs from the 21-day line, meaning the session's high stayed beneath it. The base sits far below the 603.88 high of Jan. 7, and the stock is 31.9% off that 52-week peak. It ranks 47 of 99 on the desk's list, its RS line is 33.6% below its high, and the stock is down 27.4% this year.

The September quarter split two ways: revenue rose 21.7% to 3.05 billion, while earnings fell 23.6% to 1.49 a share, down from 2.29, 2.28 and 2.21 in the three prior quarters. Next earnings are due Jan. 21. The market cap is about 142.44 billion and the forward P/E is 32.96.
Zacks noted the stock is down 1.7% since its last earnings report.
A close under 405.44 would turn this into a failed breakout back inside the base.
article.watch: Whether 411.02 holds above the 405.44 buy point, and whether the stock can retake the 50-day line at 422.99.

article.deck: A stalled breakout: Microsoft sits 9.2% below its 553.82 deep-cup buy point and under the 50-day line, so there is no entry now.
body: Microsoft fell 5.59, or 1.1%, to 502.70 as of 11:43 a.m. Mountain and is trading under its 50-day line at 520.15. The stock broke out of a 51-week deep cup, 36.9% deep, past a 553.82 buy point on Nov. 4, when it traded 2.3x its average volume. Eleven sessions later it is 9.2% below the buy point, well out of the buy range that ran to 581.51. Today's volume is on pace for 0.99x its 50-day average.

The stock is 3.4% under the 50-day line and 3.7% under the 21-day at 521.82, with an ATR reading of 0.0 from the 21-day line. It remains 13.4% above the 200-day line at 443.20 and 10.1% below its 52-week high of 559.15. Microsoft ranks 67 of 99 on the desk's list, and its RS line is 6.8% below its high. The stock is up 3.9% this year and 1.8% over twelve months.

The September quarter was strong: earnings rose 32.3% to 4.92 a share and revenue rose 18.8% to 92.28 billion. Revenue has climbed across the four quarters given, from 81.27 billion to 82.89 billion, 90.01 billion and 92.28 billion. Next earnings are due Jan. 27. The market cap is about 3.73 trillion and the forward P/E is 20.75.

Benzinga reported Satya Nadella saying that selling AI capacity to just one or two customers 'is not a business,' and Jefferies said after Ignite meetings that Microsoft is well positioned to weather an AI slowdown.
A move back over the 50-day line would be the first repair; the breakout stays stalled while the stock is under 553.82.
article.watch: Whether Microsoft can reclaim the 50-day line at 520.15 on the way back toward the 553.82 buy point.

body: Palo Alto Networks traded at 369.20 before the open, up 29.28, or 8.6%, as of 8:50 a.m. Eastern. That came on top of Wednesday, when the stock closed at 339.92, up 30.63, or 9.9%, and traded 2.83x its 50-day average volume. The chart is a six-week cup, 30.3% deep, with a rim on Oct. 6 and a low on Nov. 17. The buy point is 432.43 and the buy range runs to 454.05. Wednesday's close sat 21.4% below the buy point.

The 52-week high is 432.33, and the close was 21.4% under it. Wednesday's close was 0.5% below the 21-day exponential average at 341.75, 0.0 ATRs from the 21-day line, with a 14-day ATR of 19.52. It ranks 96 of 99 on the desk's list for relative strength, and the RS line is 13.6% off its high. The stock is up 84.5% this year and 67.5% over the past year.

The quarter ended July 31 brought a loss of 35 cents a share against a profit a year earlier, an EPS change of -197.2%, on revenue of $3.41 billion, up 34.4%. EPS ran 0.47, 0.61, -0.22 and -0.35 over the four quarters given, while revenue climbed each quarter from $2.474 billion. The market values the company at about $278.3 billion, at 69.3 times forward earnings. The next earnings date is Feb. 16, 2027.
